What We Do

Communities built the coast.
We help them stay.

Coastal communities face a compounding crisis: floods that arrive faster, heat that lingers longer, and displacement that tears apart the social fabric that kept people safe for generations. Harbor Steps was founded on a single conviction — that access to preparation should not depend on income.

We partner directly with residents, local emergency managers, schools, and housing advocates to deliver practical tools, training, and resources where they're needed most — before disaster strikes.

Our Work

Four programs,
one mission

From backyard flood kits to cross-county relocation support — our programs meet communities where they are.

Flood Ready Neighborhoods

Community-level flood preparedness training and sealed emergency kits delivered to households in vulnerable zip codes. Each kit includes waterproof document storage, a 72-hour supply plan, and access to a trained neighborhood coordinator.

12,400 kits distributed · 9 states

Climate Migration Network

Legal aid, relocation counseling, and housing placement services for families facing permanent displacement due to repeated flooding or uninhabitable heat. We keep communities intact by prioritizing resettlement in neighboring areas with existing social ties.

1,840 families served · $3.1M in housing aid facilitated

Coastal Schools Initiative

Climate science and emergency preparedness curriculum deployed across 47 schools in Gulf Coast and Southeast Atlantic districts. Students learn to read flood maps, create family response plans, and become youth resilience ambassadors in their neighborhoods.

47 schools · 22,000 students enrolled

Heat Harbor Centers

A network of 23 community cooling and resilience centers providing refuge, supplies, medical triage, and coordination during extreme heat events and post-storm recovery. Staffed 24/7 during declared emergencies, open 6 days a week year-round.

23 centers · 340,000 visits recorded in 2024

Common questions

Yes. Harbor Steps is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit registered in the United States (EIN 84-2917650). All donations are tax-deductible to the extent permitted by law. You will receive an email receipt immediately after your gift.

We prioritize low-income coastal zip codes with documented flood risk in FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program data and surface heat indexes above EPA warning thresholds. We partner with local emergency managers to confirm community readiness before launching a program.

Yes — after checkout, you can note a program preference (Flood Ready Neighborhoods, Climate Migration Network, Coastal Schools Initiative, or Heat Harbor Centers). Unrestricted gifts allow us to direct funds where they are most urgent at any given moment.

Log in to your donor portal at giving.harborsteps.org, or email donors@harborsteps.org and we will make the change within 24 hours — no questions asked. We will never make it difficult to cancel.

Our 2024 Annual Report, IRS Form 990, and audited financial statements are downloadable from harborsteps.org/transparency. We have published complete financials every year since our founding in 2019.
